overview: Botswana's femtech scene is thin and largely research and public-health led rather than startup driven. Its real strength is women's public health: a strong HPV and cervical cancer program, a gold-tier record on eliminating mother-to-child HIV transmission, universal free sanitary pads in schools since 2017, and active PrEP research for pregnant and breastfeeding women. Emerging maternal and telemedicine ventures exist but early-stage founder activity is mostly channeled through the Standard Chartered Women in Tech accelerator in Gaborone.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent milestones concentrate on HIV, maternal health and women-led enterprise support.

items.text: Botswana advances to gold tier on the path to eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, reaching WHO paediatric-infection and service-coverage targets.
BSRHI presents PrEP Choice study findings and the upcoming STEP-UP study at the Ministry of Health PrEP Technical Working Group.
Standard Chartered Botswana awards over P700,000 in equity-free seed funding to six women-led enterprises at the second Women in Tech graduation.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Government action centers on menstrual dignity, digital health and HIV prevention.

items.text: Parliament makes all school-aged girls eligible for free sanitary pads in public and private schools.
National eHealth Strategy 2020-2024 approved, committing the Ministry of Health to ICT for health.
Botswana HIV Prevention Road Map 2023-2025 prioritizes at-risk young women and ARV-based prevention including PrEP.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Activity clusters around accelerators, telemedicine pilots and university research outreach.

items.text: Women in Tech Botswana (Standard Chartered plus Dream Factory Foundation) runs five-month cohorts backing women-led health and tech ventures in Gaborone since 2024.
Telemedicine startups extend maternal and pediatric care to rural Botswana, partnering with government, NGOs and local clinics despite connectivity gaps.
Ministry of Health hosts a digital health implementation workshop pushing Electronic Medical Records across the public sector.
BSRHI intensifies community outreach on contraception, STIs and HIV prevention through school talks and a youth leadership symposium in 2025.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
